I only once heard the noises of a beating in the corridor, and later I saw that the man who had been beaten was dead, and he lay there for two days. Who did this I don't know." Is that what it says in this statement?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Do you see the contradiction?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You don't?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Well, he was lying there from the first day. I don't say he was dead.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I leave some time for Mr. Praljak now. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just have five minutes left, because there will be another case heard in this courtroom this afternoon. So please be brief. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saric, for the sake of time, as regards telecommunications in the former Yugoslavia, the centre for communications with the world was Belgrade, yes?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: No. There was also Ljubljana, Zagreb, and Skopje, who had direct lines to other countries. The largest international switchboard was in Belgrade, but there were also international switchboards in Ljubljana with direct connections to Austria and Italy, in Zagreb with connections to Hungary, and in Skopje which had connections with Greece and Bulgaria.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But Belgrade controlled all communications?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes, Belgrade had absolute control.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So the network was concentrated towards the republican centres; Sarajevo, Popo [phoen], Bosnia-Herzegovina, Zagreb for Croatia, and so on. These were the transit centres.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And they were connected with coaxial cables to start with?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And these are cables which can transmit large numbers of telephone conversations all at once.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: After that, electromagnetic waves, high frequency electromagnetic waves were used, and let it be said they have a very small angle. They cannot go behind a hill.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So they need relays from hill to hill until they come to the end user; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In 1992, the Serbs destroyed the bridge in Rastani and the relay at Velez, thereby cutting off all communication between Mostar and the world; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: No. There was also the western part towards Stolac, but I know what you're trying to say.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, but for the most part towards Sarajevo, Jablanica, Konjic there was nothing, and then they hit the AXI central switchboard.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So then it was moved -- it was moved to avoid being completely destroyed by bombing, and in this way communication between Mostar and the rest of the world disappeared.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Partly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And the two lines which we call "parica," which were going underneath the customs bridge, and when that fell, there was a cut-off in telephone communications.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So the HVO brought a coaxial cable which they set up between Mostar and Siroki Brijeg and then they set up a relay towards Sveti Juraj overlooking Makarska, and from Makarska to Split.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: A coaxial cable can have a greater or smaller capacity; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's expensive.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: It's sensitive.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So a smaller capacity cable was laid. It wasn't very well-protected.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: It was portable.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, and a very small number of numbers, starting 058 Mostar, existed for links to Split and so on.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: 120 at the most.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, 120 at the most. All communications with Central Bosnia had also been cut off.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you couldn't reach that by phone, that area. You -- well, there were attempts in Tomislavgrad and elsewhere to try and link up because they had been oriented towards Sarajevo and now they were trying to reach Split.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: That was the situation in 1992 when we managed to beat back the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: There were no public telephone lines. Those 120 telephone numbers were very fiercely contested. People vied for those numbers, and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had some of those telephone numbers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In that army, in Vranica, you concentrated the two strongest, most important headquarters of the 4th Corps, which from -- went from Konjic and Jablanica to Stolac and the 41st Mountain Brigade, and you put that -- and you were one of the most important people in that staff. You were the chief of communications; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I have no further questions. Thank you for this information.

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I have just one question to conclude this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, sir, but we have to make use of your knowledge. One more question. The situation you just confirmed when asked by Mr. Praljak, the public telephone network between Herzegovina and other parts of Bosnia-Herzegovina, after 1992 when it was damaged, did it ever start functioning again?

utterances.speaker: IBRAHIM SARIC
utterances.text: No. Not for the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have now finished. If you have just one last question, all right.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I only wanted to say that after the cross-examination of General Praljak, Dr. Prlic's Defence has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the exhibits to be tendered by the Defence are concerned, do you have any additional requests in that area? Ms. Nozica?

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I tender document 2D 00083, and I tender document -- the document we received from the Prosecutor, RR 043775, and RR 043776, which could not be seen in e-court, and we can check on Monday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Our team wishes to tender 5D 00515. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one thing about General Petkovic's Defence: The document we tender was received by the Defence from the OTP. This is not a document we obtained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, on Monday I will ask you for five minutes for the following reason: As for the computer I need in the Detention Unit is no longer an issue of reason. I wish to address Your Honours in this respect because I no longer wish to yield in this respect. I do have the right to prepare my defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We shall talk about this again on Monday. I'd like to thank you, Mr. Saric. On behalf of the Bench, we would like to thank you for having come to testify. We wish you a safe journey home. And we shall meet again next week on Monday at a quarter past 2.00, in line with the schedule that has been prepared by the Prosecution, and everybody has had a copy of this. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 21st day of August, 2006, at 2.15 p.m. 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.48 p.m.,
